title: CIA and at least two other US intelligence bodies reportedly hit in breach of an open-source intelligence system, per NYT via Korrespondent
date_note: Korrespondent.net's article of 25 November gives no earlier day; it says the breach was discovered "recently" per the New York Times report of 24 November.
summary: Korrespondent.net, citing the New York Times, reports a breach of an open-source intelligence analysis system used by the CIA and at least two other US intelligence bodies, including the NGA and the ODNI. Sources told the NYT classified material was not at risk and the problem is fixed. Two NYT sources said preliminary indicators, including the AI tool Artex, may point to China. No government statement is reported.
plain: A Ukrainian outlet, citing the New York Times, says hackers got into an open-source analysis system used by the CIA and two other US agencies. No official statement is reported.
exec: Anonymous sources told the NYT, per Korrespondent.net, that classified material was not at risk; the breach is not officially confirmed.
geo_basis: US federal intelligence agencies; the article gives no city

validation.note: Only Korrespondent.net read, relaying an anonymously sourced NYT report; the NYT page was not found or read; no government statement.
